Subject: Rushmore impact — initial ops triage

Team — quick summary of what I’m seeing from the runtime side:
- Around 08:45 PDT an automated rollout of a new tenant burst policy (config change INF-4318) went to full traffic for the multi-tenant pool. The policy introduced a smaller per-tenant burst window (200 tokens) but a shared corridor for short bursts.
- Rushmore’s traffic pattern includes frequent short spikes that now collide with the new corridor; the token bucket is being drained and requests are being reclassified as quota-exceeded instead of queued. That aligns with the 429s Samir attached.
- We have a short-term mitigation: increase Rushmore’s per-tenant burst allowance to the previous level (500 tokens) and pin them to the old burst policy for 2 hours while we validate. This requires a config change and a controlled restart on the serving pool (non-blocking).

I’ve attached the policy dump and the rollout details (rushmore_rate_policy_dump.json). Connor — can you confirm the risk profile of the pin and estimate the time to implement? Rafael / Laura — please confirm if Rushmore wants the immediate pin and whether we should offer SLA credit preliminarily.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Service Ops, Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 17 Apr 2025 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rushmore impact — initial ops triage

Confirming Marissa’s diagnosis after looking at tenant logs and the serving traces:
- Logs show repeated token-bucket replenishment races at sub-1s intervals for Rushmore’s token pool. The new corridor uses a shared refill cadence which, under Rushmore’s bursty pattern, causes momentary exhaustion and immediate 429s rather than allowing short queuing.
- Proposed hotfix: pin Rushmore to the legacy burst profile (revert per-tenant window to 500 tokens) and add a temporary exception that routes their short bursts to the dedicated low-latency pool (pool-b). Roll-forward plan: revert pin after we finish a telemetry sweep (2h), then deploy a corrected corridor algorithm that factors tenant burst profiles (INF-4335).
- Risk: slight increase in per-token CPU usage while routed to pool-b; we should notify capacity management and add short-term quota protection to avoid cross-tenant impact. I estimate ~18 minutes to flip the pin and routing change, plus 5–10 minutes of verification.

Connor O’Brien
SRE, Serving Runtime

Samir — update and immediate mitigation:

What we did:
- Pinned Rushmore to the previous burst profile (500-token per-tenant window) and routed short bursts to a low-latency pool. This action was performed at 13:18 PDT and validated by ops.
- Immediate effect: dropped 429 rate fell ~92% for the next 90 minutes in our telemetry, and p95 latency returned to baseline for most paths.

Next steps:
- We’ll keep Rushmore pinned for 2 hours while Connor and Marissa run a telemetry sweep to ensure no bleed-through.
- Permanent fix: INF-4335 (corridor algorithm change) scheduled for the next minor release; ETA 2025-04-22.
- We will initiate an SLA review with Laura to evaluate credits; I understand the business impact and will prioritize that conversation.

Temporary workarounds (if you see further issues): 1) reduce simultaneous parallel calls from your workers for 10 minutes; 2) fall back to the lower-throughput endpoint /v1/stream (less parallelism). Either is a short-term stopgap while we verify.

Please let me know if you want an executive sync tonight — we can set a 30-min call.

-Rafael
